nodes.summary: Two lattice cells $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ are face adjacent when there is an axis $k$ such that $x_j = y_j$ for every axis $j \ne k$ and $|x_k - y_k| = 1$.
nodes.title: Face adjacency of lattice cells

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $n$, $A_d(n)$ is the number of fixed $n$-cell polycubes in dimension $d$, that is, the number of $n$-cell polycubes in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that are in canonical position.
nodes.title: Number of fixed polycubes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $n$, the fixed $n$-cell polycubes in dimension $d$ are represented by the finite sets $S$ of lattice cells in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that are polycubes (nonempty and connected through face adjacency), have exactly $n$ cells, and are in canonical position (the minimum of each coordinate over $S$ is $0$).
nodes.title: Fixed polycubes

nodes.summary: A finite set $S$ of lattice cells in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is in canonical position when, for every axis $k$, every cell $x \in S$ has $x_k \ge 0$ and some cell $x \in S$ has $x_k = 0$; that is, the minimum of each coordinate over $S$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Canonical position of a cell set

nodes.summary: A finite set $S$ of lattice cells in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is a polycube when it is nonempty and any two cells $x, y \in S$ are joined by a finite sequence of cells of $S$, starting at $x$ and ending at $y$, in which consecutive cells are face adjacent.
nodes.title: Polycube

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a lattice cell in dimension $d$ is a point of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, that is, a function assigning an integer to each of the $d$ coordinate axes.
nodes.title: Lattice cells

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 1$, let $A_d(n)$ be the number of fixed $n$-cell polycubes in dimension $d$, and for each $i$ let $\mathrm{DX}(n,i)$ be the number of fixed $n$-cell polycubes proper in dimension $i$. Then
nodes.title: Lunnon's dimension decomposition for fixed polycubes

nodes.summary: The proper dimension of a finite set $S$ of lattice cells in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is the number of axes $k$ on which $S$ varies, that is, for which there are cells $x, y \in S$ with $x_k \ne y_k$.
nodes.title: Proper dimension

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, $\mathrm{DX}(n,i)$ is the number of fixed $n$-cell polycubes proper in dimension $i$, that is, of fixed $n$-cell polycubes in dimension $i$ whose proper dimension is $i$.
nodes.title: Number of proper fixed polycubes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, the fixed $n$-cell polycubes proper in dimension $i$ are the fixed $n$-cell polycubes in dimension $i$ whose proper dimension is $i$, that is, which vary along each of the $i$ axes.
nodes.title: Proper fixed polycubes

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
